summary: Wallabag is a self-hosted read-it-later application that fetches web pages and strips away clutter to provide a clean reading interface. It falls under archiving and digital preservation by letting you retain local copies of online content for future access.
goodFor: It suits users who want to store offline copies of web articles rather than relying on commercial third-party bookmarking services.
watchOut: You will need to maintain your own instance and manage updates, and it competes with mature, well-known alternatives like Pocket or browser-native reading modes.
deployNotes: As a PHP application, it typically requires a web server like Nginx or Apache, a separate database such as MySQL or PostgreSQL, and persistent storage for any cached assets.
